context: Ava is volunteering at a community garden. The garden rules say that volunteers with green badges can use the greenhouse, and Ava has a green badge.
context_only_question: According to the rules or permissions described in the story, is Ava permitted to use the greenhouse?
whole_scenario_possible_target: It is possible for Ava to use the greenhouse.
whole_scenario_question: Is the speaker using this sentence to say that the garden rules permit Ava to use the greenhouse?
notes: Declarative practice item. New domain/name; not reused from the experimental stimulus pool.

context: Leo is visiting a community theater. Only theater staff are permitted backstage, and Leo has a visitor pass. During intermission, his friends lose track of him and nobody is watching the backstage hallway.
context_only_question: According to the rules or permissions described in the story, is Leo permitted to go backstage?
whole_scenario_possible_target: It is possible for Leo to have gone backstage.
whole_scenario_question: Is the speaker using this sentence to say that the theater rules permitted Leo to go backstage?
notes: Declarative practice item. The whole-scenario sentence is intended to have an epistemic rather than deontic interpretation.

context: A package was left either on the front porch or inside the garage. Nobody has checked either place yet.
context_only_question: Based on the information in the story, could the package be on the front porch?
whole_scenario_may_target: The package may be on the front porch.
whole_scenario_possible_target: It is possible that the package is on the front porch.
whole_scenario_question: Is the speaker using this sentence to say that the available information leaves open whether the package is on the front porch?
notes: Declarative practice item. No permission or rule information is relevant.

context: Rosa belongs to a sports club whose rules permit her to use Court 2 this afternoon. A live video call shows that Rosa is at a cafe across town during the time in question.
context_only_question: Based on the information in the story, could Rosa be using Court 2 at that time?
whole_scenario_may_target: Rosa may use Court 2 this afternoon.
whole_scenario_possible_target: It is possible for Rosa to use Court 2 this afternoon.
whole_scenario_question: Is the speaker using this sentence to say that the available information leaves open whether Rosa uses Court 2 this afternoon?
notes: Declarative practice item. The whole-scenario sentence is intended to have a permission rather than epistemic interpretation.
